A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoDoL and contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting comparison. Both were inspected through their final reference pages; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoDoL classification experiments, component and context-length ablations, domain-information sensitivity tests, and alignment visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds quantitative alignment results across four benchmarks.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 revises the stated token fusion from concatenation with a doubled-size representation to explicit per-token elementwise addition in v2 Equation 5. The overall CLIP-and-DMN framework remains. Some v2 prose still says concatenation, and the PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, and DigitDG, retaining the same multiple-domain, single-domain, and partial-domain-information scenarios. The new alignment and retrieval diagnostics evaluate existing benchmark test domains rather than introducing new data coverage.

E2.justification: The alignment comparison expands from CoOp in Figure 6 to zero-shot CLIP, CoOp, and CoCoOp in v2 Table 6. Comparator membership in the main classification comparisons, Tables 1–3, is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4.4 adds three alignment evaluation metrics: matched-versus-mismatched cosine similarity gap, embedding-centroid modality gap, and image-to-prompt Recall@1. Existing classification protocols, backbones, batch size, training epochs, and context-length grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantial quantitative examination of the central alignment explanation across all four benchmarks using three diagnostics, supplementing v1's small PACS visualization. Existing DMN/CMN ablations and domain-information sensitivity tests remain. Tables 4–5 detail existing context-length analyses rather than establishing new ablation designs.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 adds uncertainty values for the default context-length setting, such as 95.31±0.45 for PACS Art Painting. Both versions already report three random seeds in Tables 1–2 and show error bars in Figure 5. The new ± quantities are not explicitly identified as standard deviations or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical numerical results. New Table 6 adds substantial alignment evidence: CoDoL averages 0.27 cosine gap, 0.61 modality gap, and 86.9 Recall@1, versus CoCoOp's 0.22, 0.71, and 84.5. Table 5 also supplies previously unreported transfer-specific context-length scores. These are added results, not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v2 Equations 7–8 explicitly define a joint posterior with a uniform 1/K domain prior and then marginalize domains, correcting the unnormalized class-probability sum in v1 Equation 6. Section 3.3 also revises the DMN tensor dimensions and token-combination formula. Neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly presents improved alignment as one contributing factor, rather than the sole cause, of observed OOD gains. The central CoDoL and DMN contributions, benchmark scope, and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the causal interpretation of alignment and interprets Table 6 as evidence that alignment improvements extend beyond PACS. It explicitly explains that inference requires no test-domain labels and adds prospective reliability and efficiency impacts. The existing storage and training-time limitation is retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 specifies the DMN output as an M_k-by-B offset tensor and explicitly documents marginalization over training-domain prompts without test-domain labels. Section 4.1 otherwise retains the same implementation settings; no code release, data-access instructions, or additional hardware details are provided.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds discussion attributed to Cheng, Chi, Zhao, and Xu et al. (2024), distinguishing CoDoL through instance conditioning, text-side prompting, and domain-marginalized inference. This is a focused positioning expansion; these added in-text citations lack corresponding full bibliography entries.

P1.justification: Most prose and the numbered section sequence remain. v2 makes localized revisions to the abstract and method explanation, expands related work, adds broader-impact and acknowledgment sections, updates authorship, and removes ACM template placeholders.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column TMLR layout. v2 adds Tables 4–6, redistributes existing tables and figures, and places Figure 6's previously stacked heatmaps side by side. The six original figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the central alignment argument with quantitative evidence, qualifies its causal interpretation, and corrects posterior normalization. These gains are limited by incomplete setup information for Table 6 and unresolved inconsistencies: Table 5 reports 95.91 for the default PACS ViT-B/16 setting versus 97.12 in Table 3, while some prose still describes concatenation despite the revised addition formula. Overall, the evidence supports a limited quality improvement.
